messages:
olivia: Quick share — ran the util-margin experiment on the canary GPU pool this morning. p50 and throughput look fine but p99 spikes when GPU util creeps above ~78%. posting condensed numbers and trace snippets.

olivia: perf summary (30m sample):
```
baseline (margin=5%): throughput=220 r/s, p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=410ms, avg_gpu_util=82%
test (margin=12%): throughput=198 r/s, p50=46ms, p95=110ms, p99=200ms, avg_gpu_util=70%
observed: p99 cut ~2x with ~10% throughput loss
```

raj: Interesting. do we have a kernel-id timeline? my hunch: kernel selector flips to fallback kernel at certain microbatch+seq combos and the fallback causes the tail.

maria: Can you paste the microbatch size distribution and seq-length breakdown? skewed microbatches + long seqs create stragglers.

olivia: microbatch histogram (per-request):
```
microbatch_size: 1: 48%
2: 30%
4: 15%
8+: 7%
seq_len bins: <64: 72%, 64-256: 22%, >256: 6%
kv_miss_rate (tail sessions): ~14%
```

dave: 14% kv miss on tails is significant. each miss forces recompute/longer kernel path and memory traffic. combined with larger microbatches it's unsurprising the p99 jumps.

raj: Kernel flip detail from profiler: when combined_token_count > ~2500 for a launch we see selector pick kernel_B (stable but ~3.8x slower on our setup for long seqs) vs kernel_A (fast but memory-hungry). That threshold is sensitive to batch composition.

olivia: here's a short trace snippet (filtered):
```
[req123] microbatch=4 seq=128 kv_hit=0 kernel=kernel_B latency=392ms
[req456] microbatch=1 seq=32 kv_hit=1 kernel=kernel_A latency=48ms
[req789] microbatch=8 seq=64 kv_hit=0 kernel=kernel_B latency=520ms
```

maria: So root causes: (1) kv misses -> heavier compute + memory traffic, (2) microbatch aggregation causes combined token triggers for kernel_B, (3) kernel_B has long tails.

dave: Proposal: two-prong experiment — A) increase util margin from 5%->12% (soft admit) B) implement soft-shed for low-priority requests when kv_miss + kernel_B predicted latency > SLO. Run A/B and measure p95/p99, throughput, and failed requests.

raj: Also propose a short-term kernel override: if seq < 64, force kernel_A even if combined token heuristic suggests kernel_B. We accept higher memory use for small seqs but keep tails down. Simple guard.

maria: Add tracing keys: kernel_id, kv_miss, combined_token_count, microbatch_size to every sampled request. will make correlations easier.

olivia: I'll schedule canary: 12% margin + soft-shed policy toggles, kernel override for seq<64 for the canary. CI bot, please schedule canary slot in eu-west at 11:30 PT.

ci-bot: scheduled canary: eng-runtime-canary-55 -> starts 2059880200, policy set: margin=12%, soft_shed=true, kernel_override.seq_lt_64=true.

raj: For the simulation side, i'll run a quick synthetic workload that reproduces heavy kv_miss tails (add 10% cold sessions with seq>128) and evaluate headroom sensitivity from 60%-86% util. will post plots.

dave: We should also validate UX impact: soft-shed path should return quick degraded response (shorter max length) rather than full failure. we'll gather error-rate and user-latency metrics.

olivia: Plan: run canary + synthetic sim in parallel. collect: p50/p95/p99, throughput, kernel-switch-rate, kv_miss correlation. I'll post results by EOD. :thumbsup:
